subject.lede: The work record is a private notebook that hands every new session a short brief about your PRs, holds and decisions. When the brief silently stops showing up, guessing why wastes a session. work-doctor is the car's diagnostic port: one command runs seven read-only checks, each naming what broke, the likely cause and the exact command that fixes it. The skill wraps it with rules about which fixes Claude may apply on its own (one) and which it must ask about (all the rest).

tldr.what: Finds out why the session brief is missing, wrong or not backed up, without changing anything.
tldr.how: One command runs seven checks in order, including a dry run of the session-start hook, and prints each problem with its cause and fix.
tldr.watch_out: It never repairs anything itself: apart from tightening the record folder's permissions, every fix waits for your yes.

context.purpose: When a new session should have received your work brief and did not, you can ask Claude "work doctor" and get the cause and the fix in one reading, instead of debugging hooks by hand.
context.why_now: The work record's hook fails open on purpose, so when it breaks it breaks silently; doctor is the only place that says so.
in_scope: The skill: when it fires, what Claude may and may not do
The doctor command: its seven checks, in order, and how it decides the exit code
The hook dry run that answers "would a session here get the brief?"
What happens when one check itself crashes
Every doctor function in scripts/work.py, in the Code reference
out_of_scope: How the work record is written (start, decide, hold, handoff)
PR state such as CI or reviews, which the record never stores
Finding a past session (the session-find skill)

entry_points.label: work-doctor skill ("brief not showing", "is my record backed up")
SessionStart hook: work_brief.py
entry_points.note: doctor runs it as a dry run; it never starts a real session

terms.means: A private folder of small event files (one per decision, hold, handoff) that outlives any one chat.
One feature family in the record: a name, the repos and the PR branches it covers.
The short summary of a workstream that the session-start hook injects into a new session.
Doctor feeds the session-start hook the exact input a real session in that folder would send, and reads what it prints.
One problem doctor reports: an id, a severity, what is wrong, the likely cause, and the fix as a command.
error and warn fail the run; info is something to accept or act on, and the run still passes.
When something goes wrong, do nothing rather than block: the hook prints no brief instead of breaking the session. Safe, but silent.
A note on a PR saying "do not push or merge this yet", with a reason. Shown in the brief.
The file list your own backup tool uses; doctor checks it names the record folder.
A Claude Code home such as ~/.claude, or a second one you point CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR at. Each has its own installed copy of the plugin.

lines.code: ctx.matches = lookup(cwd)            # which workstream is this folder?
for check_id, fn in CHECKS:          # registered by @check, in source order
except: found = [crashed(check_id)]  # one broken check never hides the rest
ok = no error and no warn

outline.title: check_brief(ctx): the hook dry run, as pseudocode

lines.code: if one workstream matches and brief is empty: error hook-silent
if brief is over its token budget: warn budget

scenarios.title: "My brief stopped showing": doctor finds the cause

steps.t: You say the session brief is not showing
steps.d: That phrase is one of the skill's triggers, so Claude loads the work-doctor rules before touching anything.

steps.t: Claude runs the doctor command for this folder
steps.d: Diagnose first: rule one forbids guessing that the hook is broken from a missing brief alone.

steps.t: Doctor works out which workstream this folder belongs to
steps.d: It matches the repo's origin remote and branch against the record. A crash here becomes a finding, not a stack trace.

steps.t: The seven checks line up in source order
steps.d: Each is a function marked with a decorator that adds it to one list. Adding a check is adding one function.

steps.t: Record checks: is the folder private, and is every event file readable?
steps.d: A folder other users can read is a warning; a broken event file is reported, never moved or deleted.

steps.t: Lookup check: this repo and branch match exactly one workstream?
steps.d: None or several is the usual reason for a missing brief, and the fix pre-fills the start command.

steps.t: Brief check: doctor dry-runs the session-start hook
steps.d: It sends the hook the exact input a real session here would send and reads the answer, so "would a session get the brief" is a yes or no, not a guess.
code: if matched and not brief: error D-brief.hook-silent

steps.t: Hooks check: does every installed plugin copy register the work hooks?
steps.d: A stale copy in one config dir runs old hooks. The fix is the exact reinstall chain, prefixed with that config dir.

steps.t: Backup and holds checks, from local state only
steps.d: Commits ahead of upstream are counted from local refs; nothing is fetched. Holds older than {{stale_days}} are listed as info.

steps.t: Doctor sorts findings, worst first, and sets the exit code
steps.d: An error or a warning makes the run fail; info alone lets it pass.

steps.t: Claude explains the finding plainly and asks before fixing
steps.d: One sentence each: what broke, why, what the fix does. Only a permissions fix on the record folder may be applied without asking.
do: the hook fails silently here; run this command?

steps.t: After the fix, Claude re-runs doctor until it exits clean
steps.d: Done is a clean doctor run, shown, not a claim that the fix worked.

scenarios.title: One check crashes; the others still report

steps.t: The brief check hits a file shape it does not expect, and raises
steps.d: Doctor exists for broken records, so a broken record must not break doctor.

steps.t: The crash becomes its own error finding
steps.d: It says the check could not finish, names the exception, and asks for a report with the JSON output.

steps.t: The remaining checks run as normal
Doctor fails the run with the crash listed first

scenarios.title: What if doctor repaired things itself?

steps.t: The events check finds an unreadable event file and deletes it
steps.d: That file may hold the only copy of a decision; the brief already skips it safely.

steps.t: The hooks check reinstalls the plugin on its own, in the wrong config dir
steps.d: Uninstall succeeds, install fails: that config dir now has no plugin at all.

steps.t: You find out later, with a decision gone and a session broken

scenarios.title: Fix: the command is read-only, and every fix is a command you approve

steps.t: The events check only reports the broken file
steps.d: Nothing in the doctor checks writes, fetches or calls GitHub; the fix is text.

steps.t: The hooks check prints the reinstall chain for the exact config dir
steps.d: The command carries that config dir, so it cannot land in the wrong one; Claude shows it and asks.

steps.t: You approve, Claude runs it, and doctor confirms
do: ran it; doctor run is clean

scenarios.title: A hold does not block a push yet

steps.t: You put a hold on a PR: do not push until the backend lands
A later session pushes the PR anyway
steps.d: The hold is shown in the brief, but no hook checks it before a push; that guard is planned for a later phase.
do: git push of the held PR goes through

steps.t: Doctor can only list the hold and its age

options.label: Read-only diagnosis; every fix is a printed command
pros: Safe to run any time, on any machine
The fix is visible and reviewable before it runs
cons: Takes one more step: someone has to run the fix

options.label: Doctor repairs what it finds
cons: Can delete the only copy of a decision
A half-finished reinstall leaves no plugin

options.label: No doctor: debug hooks by hand
cons: The hook fails open, so nothing says it broke

decision.deciding_factor: The record is private and some repairs cannot be undone, so the diagnosis must never be the thing that breaks it.
decision.revisit_when: A repair proves both common and fully reversible, like the folder permissions fix already is.

checks.q: How can doctor know whether a new session here would get the brief, without starting one?
checks.answer: It runs the session-start hook itself with the exact input a real session would send, and reads what it prints.

checks.q: The brief check just crashed. Does doctor stop?
checks.answer: No: the crash becomes an error finding and the other checks still run.
Claude, but only after showing you the exact command and you saying yes.

notes.check: Decorator: adds a check function to the CHECKS list under its id, in source order.
notes.finding: Builds one finding: id, severity, what is wrong, the likely cause, the fix.
notes.check_record: D-record: is the record switched off, missing, not a folder, or readable by other users?
notes.check_events: D-events: reports event files that cannot be read or parsed, and never touches them.
notes.check_lookup: D-lookup: does this folder's repo and branch match exactly one workstream?
notes.check_brief: D-brief: dry-runs the session hook here; flags a silent hook, a slow one, or a brief over its token budget.
notes.reinstall_cmd: The exact uninstall, marketplace update and install chain, prefixed with the config dir it is for.
notes.check_hooks: D-hooks: do this plugin and each installed copy register the work hooks?
notes.check_backup: D-backup: does the backup hint name the record folder, and is the backup repo pushed and not mid-rebase?
notes.check_holds: D-holds: lists holds older than the stale threshold, as info.
notes.crashed: Turns an exception inside a check into an error finding, so the other checks still report.
notes.run_doctor: Runs the lookup, then every check in order; sorts findings worst first and decides ok.
notes.print_doctor: Prints the header (record dir, workstream, dry-run result), each finding with cause and fix, and a summary.
notes.cmd_doctor: The command: checks the folder argument, runs doctor, prints text or JSON, and exits with success only when nothing failed.

notes.main: Returns the session-start brief for the folder when it matches exactly one workstream; nothing otherwise.
